answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with work-history reputation: trust is earned only by completing attested tasks, and scores decay over time so idle identities sink toward their nadir. A fresh identity starts with zero weight, like uncut quartz, and must accumulate many costly verified contributions before reaching the zenith of full influence. Creating thousands of Sybils therefore buys nothing, because each one faces the same long, expensive climb, while honest agents keep their proven standing.
